title: Unified Field Bosonization Technique for strongly inhomogenous Luttinger Liquids
authors: Soundarya P, Venkata Suryanarayana M, Joy Prakash Das
abstract: We introduce the Unified Field Bosonization Technique (UFBT), a direct bosonization framework for strongly inhomogeneous one-dimensional Luttinger liquids (LLs) containing static impurities. UFBT incorporates impurity scattering through a symmetrized combination of bosonic phase fields and yields closed-form expressions for arbitrary N-point correlation functions for a broad class of static impurity potentials, including delta barriers, finite barriers and finite wells. The formalism requires neither renormalization-group analysis nor perturbative expansions, providing an analytical description of the inhomogeneous system at the bosonized level. The technique is validated by recovering known limiting cases, showing agreement with the first-order perturbative expansion in the interaction strength, and demonstrating consistency with the Schwinger-Dyson equations. A key result is that the correlation function exponents remain independent of the impurity strength, while the impurity dependence is captured by the spatial structure and amplitudes of the correlation functions. The resulting correlation functions establish a foundation for analytical studies of transport, Friedel oscillations, and the local and dynamical density of states in strongly inhomogeneous Luttinger liquids.
summary: This work introduces the Unified Field Bosonization Technique (UFBT) to analytically calculate correlation functions in strongly inhomogeneous Luttinger Liquids. The technique successfully handles static impurities without relying on perturbative expansions or renormalization group methods. It provides universal results for correlation exponents while accurately capturing the spatial structure imposed by the impurities.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop an analytical method to calculate correlation functions in strongly inhomogeneous one-dimensional Luttinger Liquids (LLs) containing static impurities.
main_result: The Unified Field Bosonization Technique (UFBT) yields closed-form expressions for N-point correlation functions, showing that correlation exponents are independent of impurity strength.
method: It introduces the UFBT, a direct bosonization framework that incorporates impurity scattering via a symmetrized combination of bosonic phase fields, avoiding RG analysis or perturbative expansions.
model_or_system: The system is an interacting electron gas modeled as a Luttinger Liquid in one dimension, perturbed by localized static impurities (barriers and wells). The Hamiltonian involves electron-electron interactions and impurity potentials.
key_observables: N-point correlation functions, single-particle Green's functions, local/dynamical density of states, and Friedel oscillations.
important_parameters: Impurity strength (characterized by reflection/transmission amplitudes), Luttinger parameter (K), and bulk velocities ($v_h, v_F$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on a generalized Fermi-Bose correspondence for strong inhomogeneity and uses the Gaussian approximation for calculating bosonized two-point functions.
paper_structure: The paper builds the formalism by first establishing the non-interacting case, then incorporating forward-scattering interactions via the DDCF, and finally deriving the full interacting Green's functions and N-point correlation functions using the UFBT.
why_interesting: The analytical treatment of strong spatial inhomogeneity in 1D correlated systems is crucial for understanding transport phenomena in nanoscale conductors, which often exhibit strong electron-electron interactions.
